definitions.explanation: Products that have been brought in from another country for sale or use.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}を{扱|あつか}っている。
examples.english: This store deals in imported goods.

examples.japanese: {輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}は{国産品|こくさんひん}より{高|たか}いことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Imported goods are often more expensive than domestic products.

examples.japanese: ヨーロッパからの{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}には{関税|かんぜい}がかかる{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: Tariffs may apply to imported goods from Europe.

notes:
{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん} is a compound of {輸入|ゆにゅう} (import) and {品|ひん} (goods). It refers to any product brought in from abroad.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}を{扱|あつか}う: to handle imported goods
- {輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}に{関税|かんぜい}がかかる: tariffs are imposed on imports
- {輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}に{頼|たよ}る: to rely on imports
- {高級|こうきゅう}{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}: high-end imported goods

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {輸出品|ゆしゅつひん}: exported goods
- {国産品|こくさんひん}: domestically produced goods

USAGE:
Often appears in discussions about trade, pricing, and consumer choices. In Japan, {輸入品|ゆにゅうひん} can carry connotations of being either luxury items (European brands) or affordable alternatives (imported food).
